name: Belmond Mount Nelson Hotel
positioning: Historic pink hotel in Cape Town, open since 1899, with garden cottage suites, a Victorian-house spa and afternoon tea
best_for: Travelers who like a historic hotel with a long story
Guests who want afternoon tea and a garden setting in the city

facts.text: Mount Nelson opened on Monday, 6 March 1899.
Mount Nelson was the first hotel in South Africa to offer hot and cold running water.
Winston Churchill, then a young war correspondent, was based at the hotel during the South African War.
The Prince of Wales Gate and palm-lined driveway were built in 1924 in honour of a visit by the Prince of Wales.
The Oasis wing was added to the main house in 1973.
The wooden chairs in the Garden Room and the Lord Nelson Room were originally deck chairs on Union-Castle Line ships.
Planet Bar spills out onto an outdoor terrace overlooking the gardens.
Librisa Spa is a day spa offering treatments in a historic Victorian house.
The Company's Garden, South Africa's oldest public gardens, is located across Orange Street from the hotel.

highlights.text: The second manager, Aldo Renato, painted the hotel pink in 1918 to celebrate the end of the First World War.
The Red Room by Chefs Warehouse, by chef Liam Tomlin, serves Pan-Asian cuisine in the underground space formerly known as The Grill Room.
Afternoon Tea has been served on the Windsor Table in the Hotel Lounge since 1989; before that it was served from a tea trolley.
A row of eight restored historic cottages on the grounds was converted into the Garden Cottage Suites in 1990.

considerations.text: Accommodation is in historic buildings, including the main house, the 1973 Oasis wing and converted cottages, rather than one modern block.
Librisa Spa is a day spa in a historic Victorian house, so it is a separate building rather than a large resort spa complex.
WhataHotel notes a traditional, formal atmosphere that may not suit casual travelers.
